why: Connecting all points with exactly one path between any two, as cheaply as possible, is a minimum spanning tree on the complete Manhattan-distance graph. Kruskal is the union-find way: sort all pair edges by cost and take each one whose ends are not yet connected. (With n <= 1000 the dense O(n^2) Prim is also a good fit.)
hints: 'Exactly one simple path between any two points' describes a tree. Which tree are you after?
A minimum spanning tree. Kruskal: consider edges from cheapest to most expensive and keep an edge only if it joins two different components; union-find answers that question.

Build all n(n - 1)/2 edges (cost, i, j), sort, union-find with path compression; stop after n - 1 merges. O(n^2 log n). Prim with an array of 'cheapest link to the tree' is O(n^2) and avoids the big edge list.
pitfalls: Building and sorting all n^2/2 edges for Kruskal works but is slow and memory-heavy in Python at n = 1000.
